evidence.field: 木部 entry; PDF p. 503, printed p. 490
evidence.text: The 木 entry calls the graph pictographic, describes its upper part as branches and lower part as roots, and gives ‘tree’ as its original sense. It lists uses for leaves, timber, wooden things, coffins, instruments in the ‘eight sounds’, the ‘wood’ phase of the Five Phases, and ‘plain/simple’. The entry does not date those uses or establish their order. I inspected the supplied page image directly; the entry and these lines are legible. PDF p. 504 (printed p. 491) continues other characters, not 木.
evidence.title: 字源, 李學勤主編, 2012; ISBN 9787552800692

evidence.field: 形義通解; early form and component analysis
evidence.text: The entry describes oracle and bronze forms as depicting a tree, with upper branches and lower roots, and gives ‘tree’ as the original sense. It reports the received 說文 analysis as 屮 above roots, then quotes Wang Yun’s objection that resemblance to 屮 does not establish it as a component and analyzes 木 as a complete-body pictograph. This supports describing the current whole graph as a tree while presenting the 屮 analysis as a historical account rather than an established decomposition.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 漢字甲骨部件分析

evidence.source: 說文解字, received text via Shuowen.org
evidence.text: The entry reads 「冒也。冒地而生。東方之行。从屮，下象其根。凡木之屬皆从木。」 It is evidence for the traditional lexicographic account, not independent paleographic confirmation of the 屮 segmentation.
evidence.title: 說文解字「木」 — Shuowen.org

evidence.source: 小學堂文字學資料庫 (Academia Sinica)
evidence.text: The record indexes oracle-bone, bronze, Chu bamboo-and-silk, and seal-script forms, including bronze catalogue reference 集成08477. Its summary describes 木 as a pictograph depicting a tree’s trunk, branches, and roots. This corroborates the broad whole-tree analysis; I did not inspect the record’s glyph images.
evidence.title: 漢字「木」：字形演變

evidence.source: Local Unihan extract; upstream page lookup
evidence.text: The supplied local row is U+6728, kMandarin, mù (pipeline/data/unihan-kmandarin-hsk1.tsv, line 294). Unicode’s official character-record URL was attempted but was inaccessible through the web tool, so this local row is recorded as a local reading check, not externally verified click-through evidence. 木 is analyzed here as a pictograph, so this reading does not establish a component sound role.

The oracle-bone phrase 《合集》5749「埶(藝)木」 is reported by CUHK as tree planting; its underlying rubbing was not inspected in this research. The absolute date of the cited example and earliest attestation of the spoken word remain unestablished.
The book and consulted paleographic sources list several senses but do not establish a dated progression among tree, leaves, wood/timber, coffin, wooden objects, and figurative senses.
